assessments.reasoning: Capture b0cffdeec4594a73a8406bb5f410b157 matches SHA-256 8467c35c94d5ab31cd6556203bd651cfa9a6c293043d1d5a7defd0c046f0a02c. The introduction, version heading and appended grant occur in one publisher artifact. The subsequent LGPL note explicitly identifies its narrower file scope.

As context, capture bf343064982441da8e8f4a0dae05ef69 confirms the appended permission’s wording and its generic reference to “the GPL license by which this project is covered.” The version number comes exclusively from Totem’s heading. The SPDX record supplies no competing edition.

challenge.method: Checked whether GPL section 9, the sample “any later version” notice, the trailing LGPL file note or the generic SPDX text changed the edition identified by the opening heading.
challenge.results: Section 9 describes conditional version choices. The later-version sample appears under “How to Apply These Terms to Your New Programs.” The trailing note specifically names src/totem-subtitle-encoding.c as relicensed to LGPL, providing a concrete counterexample to a project-wide inference. SPDX’s generic paragraph leaves the GPL version unspecified. All four observations are consistent with the same-file GPL version 2 finding.

limitations: A later-version election, a file-level GPL-2.0-only or GPL-2.0-or-later designation, and the base for another project’s use each require their own evidence. The 2008 SPDX name supplies no base-version or adoption-date evidence.
reasoning: Totem’s opening comment directs readers to the exception at the bottom of the file. The immediately following heading reads “GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE” and “Version 2, June 1991.” The GStreamer paragraph near the end calls its permission “above and beyond” the GPL permissions. Together these passages establish GPL version 2 as the edition printed with this exception. SCES requires a separate basis for extending that finding to another edition or file.
